title: task edit has no expected-revision precondition for concurrent writers
description:
Raised by opum-agent (2026-09-13, durable copy OPAG-120) from a live proof-graph inspection. Narrow, precise gap: Quest's existing contract already covers most of concurrent-write safety -- a write conflict returns exit 5, and the documented protocol already tells callers to re-read and run their own bounded retry. What is missing is a PRECONDITION, not the signal: a caller has no way to say 'apply this edit only if the record is still at the revision I read', so two sessions can each successfully append to the same task, and one of them silently reasoned from a stale snapshot -- no conflict is ever raised because nothing checked.

Proposed (opum-agent's framing, not settled here): an expected-revision or content-digest precondition on task edits and on batch decompositions, checked and failing BEFORE any state change, so the caller can re-read and re-apply without clobbering the other session's update.

opum-agent's own honest framing, worth keeping: this is a nice-to-have that becomes important once concurrent sessions write the same task routinely -- which the fleet does not do much of today. Scope and priority accordingly.

acceptanceCriteria.text: quest task edit accepts an optional expected-revision (or content-digest) precondition
a task edit whose precondition does not match the records current revision fails before any state change, with an exit code distinguishable from an ordinary validation error
the failure response names the current revision so the caller can re-read without a second round trip
task edit-batch supports the same precondition per operation, not only whole-task edit
existing callers that omit the precondition are unaffected -- this is additive, not a required field

plan: 1. Read tasks.ts edit()/editOn(), editBatch(), the CLI edit dispatch in main.ts, and the command-contract/command-help manifests to find the existing expectedRevision/exit-5 conflict machinery to reuse.

2. Add an optional TaskEditOptions.ifRevision to TaskService.edit/editOn: checked against the freshly-read snapshot.revision BEFORE any other work, returning the existing TaskWriteConflict shape (no new error type) on mismatch.

3. Add the same per-item ifRevision precondition to TaskService.editBatch, checked against the batch entry revision before that items row is touched; a mismatch fails only that item, same as any other per-item validation error.

4. Expose revision on task view --json only (new TaskService.viewWithRevision, one readAll call) -- additive field, not on task edit/create output, to keep the diff scoped and avoid collision with the parallel QCLI-276 task view work.

5. Wire --if-revision through main.ts (editFlags allowlist, command-help.ts flags+summary, command-contract.ts task view fields) and the per-item ifRevision JSONL field through task edit-batch, updating every golden fields-list mirror (command-contract.test.ts, src/contract/tracker/fixtures.ts, src/contract/tracker/index.ts probe table).

6. Plumb TaskWriteConflict.actualRevision from recordFromMutation/taskFromMutation out to main.ts diagnostic input via a new TrackerWriteConflictError, so the exit-5 response names the current revision (AC2) instead of discarding it as the old bare Error did.

7. Add regression tests: unit-level editOn ifRevision test against MemoryTasks, and end-to-end CLI tests proving two concurrent edits from the same read -- one wins, one gets exit 5 naming the actual revision -- plus edit-batch per-item behavior.

8. Run bun run check to green, including reconciling the QCLI-264/QCLI-265 wrapper-shape invariant test which explicitly banned a top-level revision field; amend it narrowly to allow only task views case, documented inline.
implementationNotes: Implemented --if-revision as an optional caller-supplied precondition, reusing the existing TaskWriteConflict/exit-5 shape rather than a new error type. TaskService.edit/editOn gained an options.ifRevision param, checked against the freshly-read snapshot.revision before any resolution or write; a mismatch returns {kind:"conflict", expectedRevision: ifRevision, actualRevision: snapshot.revision, operationId, ownedPaths: []} through the same TaskMutationResult channel every other write conflict already uses. editBatch got the per-item counterpart (ifRevision per JSONL line), checked against the batch entry revision before that item touches its row; a mismatch fails only that item (message: task_revision_precondition_failed, naming both expected and actual revision), matching how every other per-item validation failure in that method already behaves -- the batch itself still exits 0.

Read side: added TaskService.viewWithRevision (one readAll, mirrors viewWithPath) and wired it into task view --json only, adding an additive top-level revision field to task.view output. Deliberately did NOT add revision to task edit/create/complete/etc. output -- out of scope for the stated ACs, and it would have forced splitting the shared task.created|task.updated response-type union for no AC-required benefit. A caller captures revision from task view and supplies it back via task edit --if-revision <revision>.

CLI wiring: --if-revision added to main.ts editFlags allowlist and command-help.ts task edit flags+summary (QCLI-147 test enforces this pairing); ifRevision added as an allowed per-item JSONL top-level key for task edit-batch (validated as an optional string, alongside reference/operationId/patch), documented in task edit-batch summary too. command-contract.ts task view fields gained revision (alphabetical), and every golden mirror of that exact fields list was updated in lockstep: test/contract/command-contract.test.ts, src/contract/tracker/fixtures.ts, and src/contract/tracker/index.ts probe() required table -- found all four occurrences by grepping the literal references/status adjacency across src and test, since that is where task views field list is duplicated verbatim in this repo (the public dependency-free src/contract/tracker module is the sanctioned in-repo mirror consumed by opum-cli-e2e-style probes; no other repository was touched).

Diagnostic plumbing (AC2): recordFromMutation/taskFromMutation used to throw a bare Error("tracker_write_conflict") on ANY write conflict, discarding TaskWriteConflict.actualRevision entirely -- so even before this task, a stale-revision failure never told the caller the current revision. Added TrackerWriteConflictError (carries actualRevision) and main.ts now special-cases instanceof it before the generic tracker_write_conflict message match, adding input.actualRevision to the exit-5 diagnostic. This benefits every existing task/draft write conflict, not only --if-revision ones -- same message/exit code as before, additive input only.

Unexpected collision found and resolved: test/qcli265-planning-and-read-shape.test.ts (QCLI-264/265) has a repo-wide invariant banning a bare top-level revision key on any command data, written specifically to stop the old internal task-plus-revision write-mutation envelope from leaking. My task view revision field tripped it. Resolved narrowly: task view is now the one explicit, documented exception in that tests per-argv assertion (wrappers list is [revision] only for task view, empty everywhere else), with a comment explaining the field is the QCLI-277 read-side capability, not the banned write-mutation leak. Did not touch the QCLI-276 task-view-handling files beyond this additive revision plumbing -- no QCLI-276 implementation branch or pull request existed at the remote at the time of this work.

Evidence for the concurrency scenario (manual, live, plus an automated version in test/cli-task-edit-if-revision.test.ts): seeded a task, captured revision R0 via task view. Caller A: task edit --if-revision R0 --summary "caller A won" -> exit 0. Caller B, reasoning from the SAME R0: task edit --if-revision R0 --summary "caller B lost" -> exit 5, error_type conflict, input.actualRevision equal to d732f854e1e013eaea85ec56a41436d9c0501c99e02edebb81d0bae332f56c92. Re-read confirmed summary stayed "caller A won" and the live revision equaled the actualRevision the conflict had already named. edit-batch per-item variant demonstrated the same way: one item with a stale ifRevision failed alone (message task_revision_precondition_failed, naming both the expected and actual revision) while its sibling item in the same batch applied and the batch itself exited 0.

bun run check final result: typecheck clean, lint 0 errors (1 pre-existing unrelated warning in test/qcli122-fourth-pass.test.ts, exit 0, not introduced by this change), format:check clean, layer:check passed for 76 source files, full test suite 489 pass / 0 fail across 57 files (4232 expect() calls), including the new test/cli-task-edit-if-revision.test.ts (5 new end-to-end tests) and an extended unit test in test/integration/tasks/tasks.test.ts.
finalSummary: Added an optional expected-revision precondition to the existing write path, reusing the exit-5 conflict machinery already in place rather than inventing a new mechanism. Read side: task view --json now returns an additive revision field (new TaskService.viewWithRevision), so a caller can capture the current revision from a plain read. Write side: task edit --if-revision <revision> and a per-item ifRevision field on task edit-batch JSONL operations check the caller-supplied value against the freshly-read snapshot revision BEFORE any resolution or write; a mismatch returns the same TaskWriteConflict shape an ordinary optimistic-concurrency race already produces (exit 5, error_type conflict), now additionally naming the actual current revision in the diagnostics input field (a plumbing gap that existed even for ordinary write conflicts before this task, fixed alongside it). Verified live with two callers reading the same revision: the first edit succeeds, the second is refused with the real current revision named, and re-reading confirms the first callers write is durably intact. Batch per-item behavior verified the same way: a stale item fails alone without blocking sibling items, matching existing per-item batch error semantics. bun run check is fully green: 489 pass, 0 fail, across 57 files.
